newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: No decision on Pacific float - Meekatharra.
newsitem.headline: No decision on Pacific float - Meekatharra.

text.p: Meekatharra Minerals Ltd said on Wednesday it did not know when a decision would be made on whether to continue plans to float 40 percent of its Pacific Goldfields Ltd on the Canadian stock exchange.
Company secretary Warwick Higgs told Reuters the company had no further information on taxation changes proposed in the May 1997 Australian budget which could impact on the proposed float.
"We have not been able to get any information as to when that legislation is likely to be put before parliament," he said, adding the decision was on hold pending clarification.
Pacific Gold is a wholly owned subsidiary of Meekatharra and formerly known as MM Gold Corporation and would hold all of Meekatharra's Indonesian gold exploration interests.
Meekatharra said in its June quarterly report that its Indonesian joint venturer, the Canadian Teck Corporation had subscribed C$3 million to acquire nine percent equity interest in MM Gold Pty Ltd.
If Meekatharra decided not to float Pacific Gold by July 2000 it would purchase the Teck interest by the issue of shares in Meekatharra to the value of C$3 million, it said.

Also in its quarterly report, the company said the contractor for the demonstration plant for the proposed US$500 million South Australian pig iron export joint venture project was expected to be selected during the September 1997 quarter.

Meekatharra said MM Gold intended to withdraw from the projects it managed and operated for its 19.8 percent stake option at the Akash joint venture projects in West Java, Indonesia, following review of unencouraging results.
At its Pandeglang project in West Java, one sample of quartz vein rock float had returned an assay of 59.4 grams per tonne gold but the in-situ source had not yet been traced.
